_comment: PINNED BASELINE — do not edit to make a gate pass. This is the production router configuration every challenger is measured against: keyword-first with the self-hosted 9B as rescue (llmops.classify_hybrid, use_model_classifier=True). Challengers are checked against BOTH their immediate incumbent AND these numbers, because a chain of individually-tolerated tier regressions can otherwise drift arbitrarily far from where the router started (measured 2026-07-25: S7 model swap SIMPLE -0.041, contested guard -0.021, cumulative -0.062 against a 0.05 tolerance). Re-pin ONLY when the owner deliberately accepts a new reference point, and record why in _pinned_reason.
_pinned_reason: RE-PINNED (owner decision) to a LIVE measurement. The first pin recorded keyword+9b_mythos_q8 at 0.705, which was REPLAYED rather than measured because no coherent 9B endpoint existed. The endpoint is now healthy — the failure was a single llama-server flag, `--repeat-penalty 0` (llama.cpp treats 1.0 as no-op; 0 is a degenerate divisor that corrupts logits), not the weights, quant, context or template. The served model is now ornith_9b, which is a materially better classifier than 9b_mythos_q8 on this instrument (accuracy 0.705 -> 0.761, MODERATE 0.417 -> 0.617, COMPLEX 0.763 -> 0.711). Pinning the stronger, live-measured configuration RAISES the bar for future promotions, which is the honest direction; it also means promotions recorded before this date were judged against an easier reference.
_provisional_note: Superseded: this baseline is MEASURED live (promotion_gate.py run without --incumbent-from, verdict_status 'measured'). The previous pin was replayed and is retained in git history.
